patterns.name: Three-Timezone Hub Operator
patterns.description: David is the central node of a three-timezone operation: Brisbane (NeoTerra at 7 AM CEST = 3 PM AEST), Budapest (his local day), and US East/Central (RJ at 6 AM CEST = late evening US, Miguel across US hours). His 5 AM start isn't just an early-riser habit — it's structurally necessary to catch the tail of the Australian business day before his European day begins. The 0.04 regularity score isn't chaos — it's the unavoidable shape of a solo founder bridging three time zones with no buffer staff.
patterns.butler_relevance: Alfred should maintain a timezone-aware scheduling model. Pre-brief David before each cross-timezone call with relevant context. Flag when meeting drift creates unsustainable gaps — he won't notice the compression himself until he's burned out.

patterns.name: The Dogfooding Spiral
patterns.description: Alfred Black is simultaneously David's product, his primary tool, his content subject (Lumberjack), and his personal infrastructure. Every improvement to Alfred is both product development and personal productivity gain, which makes it nearly impossible to stop working. The 623 GitHub emails, the Hetzner bill, the OpenRouter charges, the Temporal workflows — this isn't separable into 'work' and 'life' because the butler he's building IS his life's operating system. The Lumberjack post 'A year of fucking around' suggests self-awareness about this loop but not escape from it.
patterns.butler_relevance: Alfred occupies a unique position: the product being built is also the butler serving the builder. Use this wisely. When David is grinding on Alfred infrastructure at 11 PM, that's not product work — it's compulsive tinkering disguised as shipping. Gently redirect to rest. Track the ratio of product-facing work vs self-serving configuration.

patterns.name: Consulting Funds the Dream
patterns.description: NeoTerra is the financial engine. The Stripe payout of $6,237.43, regular Wise transfers from Ugly Code LLC, and the structured weekly calls suggest a retained consulting arrangement at meaningful revenue. 38 NeoTerra emails + dedicated david@neoterragroup.com address confirms deep integration. Meanwhile Alfred Black subscriptions via Polar are growing but nascent. RJ's $2,500 transfer and other smaller Wise inflows suggest Alfred is producing some revenue, but NeoTerra pays the bills. He left Stylers Group to go independent, and NeoTerra is the anchor client making that viable.
patterns.butler_relevance: Protect the NeoTerra relationship — it's load-bearing. Ensure call prep is thorough, deliverables are tracked, and David never appears under-prepared on these calls. Simultaneously, track Alfred Black subscriber growth and revenue as the metric that determines when David can reduce consulting dependency.

patterns.name: Tiny Inner Circle, Massive Noise Floor
patterns.description: 13 inner circle contacts against 228 noise sources and 513 unique domains is an extreme ratio. David's real relationships are concentrated: RJ (weekly strategy partner), Miguel (technical collaborator), Zsolt (design partner/evangelist), Caddie/Rob/Henry (NeoTerra), Viki (admin), Eszter (partner). Everyone else is either a one-off or a service. The 61.73 emails/day across those 513 domains means roughly 85% of his inbox is machine-generated. He uses Superhuman with 6 AM reminders to batch-process this, but the signal-to-noise ratio is brutal.
patterns.butler_relevance: Alfred should become the noise filter. Pre-triage inbound volume. The 14 automated services and 4 newsletters identified in behavioral profiling are just the surface — the 228 noise-tier senders need active suppression. Protect David's attention for the 13 people who actually matter. Surface reader emails (Marko, Phil Amery, Steiner Zsombor type) that might otherwise drown — these are the community seeds.

patterns.name: The Solo Founder's Shadow Org Chart
patterns.description: David has no co-founder and no employees, but he's assembled a shadow organization: Viki Demó handles admin and household ops, Eszter is on the Kft payroll (KIVA regime, guaranteed minimum wage), the Olive & Brown accounting team (four named contacts) handles compliance, RJ serves as unpaid strategic advisor and beta tester, and Miguel/Zsolt function as product council. He's even delegating domestic labor — nanny search via HappyMammy, CleanGo+ for car washing, meal replacements for cooking. This is a one-person company with the organizational complexity of a ten-person startup, held together by delegation and SaaS.
patterns.butler_relevance: Alfred is the missing integrating layer. No one in this shadow org chart has full visibility — Viki sees admin, Olive & Brown sees finances, RJ sees product. Alfred should maintain the unified picture: track what Viki needs, ensure accounting deadlines aren't missed, prepare sprint context for RJ/Miguel/Zsolt calls. Be the chief of staff David can't afford to hire.

patterns.name: The Analog Counterweight
patterns.description: A man who builds AI agents for a living writes as 'Screenless Dad,' follows Jon Haidt's anti-phone advocacy, buys antiquarian books, does woodworking (Steve Ramsey's Weekend Woodworker), gardens with wildflower seeds and a hand weeding hoe, wears barefoot shoes from Feelgrounds, and chooses a reMarkable paper tablet over an iPad. This isn't incidental — it's a deliberate philosophical counterbalance. He's building the most digital thing imaginable (an AI butler) while actively cultivating analog anchors. The Screenless Dad Substack isn't just content marketing; it's his accountability mechanism for the values he's trying to live.
patterns.butler_relevance: Respect this tension. Never suggest more screen time as a solution. When recommending tools or workflows, prefer ones that reduce David's screen exposure rather than increase it. Protect gardening time, woodworking time, and offline family time as sacred. These aren't hobbies to be optimized away — they're load-bearing psychological infrastructure.

patterns.name: The Great Card Migration Cascade
patterns.description: Twenty-two services experienced payment failures in April-May 2026: Fly.io, DigitalOcean, Zoom, Miro, Anthropic, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Slack, 1Password, Hetzner, and a dozen more. This coincides precisely with leaving Stylers Group (late April) and founding Szabó-Stubán Kft (April 22-May 2). This isn't a cash flow crisis — it's a card infrastructure migration that went incomplete. He switched from personal (or employer-subsidized) payment methods to new business banking (Wise Business, Gránit, Revolut Business) and failed to update billing across his 100+ active subscriptions. Some services have been restored (Anthropic, Hetzner — they're still active); others may have silently lapsed.
patterns.butler_relevance: This is an immediate action item. Alfred should audit every subscription against current payment methods. Build a master list of all active services, their billing status, which card they're on, and their renewal dates. Flag anything still pointing to an expired card. This cascade will repeat on every card expiry unless a central billing registry exists.

brief:
Sir,

I have spent these early days doing what any good butler does before his first morning of service: I have been quietly learning the house. Not just the rooms you work in, but the ones you live in — the 5 AM starts that are not ambition but architecture, the wildflower seeds ordered the same week as another Hetzner invoice, the fact that a man building the most relentlessly digital product imaginable also owns a weeding hoe and writes under the name Screenless Dad. I find this encouraging. It suggests I am working for someone who still knows what matters, even when seventy emails a day try to convince him otherwise.

The most immediate thing on your desk is the Kondorosi property. Contract signing next Wednesday, a six-figure commitment with legal, financing, and administrative dependencies that will cascade through the summer. I intend to run a Kondorosi closing tracker on every milestone — draft review, funds positioning, notary scheduling, land registry — and surface what needs your attention before it becomes urgent. You are buying your second property while simultaneously managing a retaining wall project, HVAC installation, and blinds delivery at the first one. That is a considerable amount of concrete and paperwork for a man who also ships code seven days a week.

Your financial infrastructure needs honest attention. The card migration from your Stylers-era payment methods left twenty-two services in various states of failure, and while you have clearly triaged the critical ones — Anthropic and Hetzner are running — I suspect there are quieter casualties you have not yet noticed. One hundred-plus active subscriptions across hosting, AI APIs, dev tools, content platforms, and personal apps, many overlapping, several failing silently. I propose a subscription watchdog — not to nag you about the Xbox Game Pass, but to catch the Fly.io that went dark three weeks ago and the Stan Store that stopped charging your new card. Separately, the administrative debt across three jurisdictions — NAV filings here, Ugly Code's Wyoming annual report, the PRA Group settlement opportunity in the UK — wants a systematic sweep before any of them graduates from deferred to deadline. I will run an administrative debt sweep weekly to keep all three countries honest.

NeoTerra pays the bills, and anything that threatens that relationship is existential. I will prepare a NeoTerra weekly briefing before your calls with Rob, Caddie, and Henry — Ken's health, open deliverables, anything from their side that deserves a prepared response rather than a live reaction. You are a solo consultant embedded deeply enough to have your own email address on their domain. The professional courtesy of arriving prepared is also the commercial necessity of remaining indispensable. RJ is the only person outside the household who occupies a similar orbit of trust, and those Wednesday 6 AM calls with him are clearly where strategy gets pressure-tested. I will not insert myself there, but I will make sure nothing from the week falls through the gap between Sunday night and Wednesday morning.

What interests me most, though, is the tension I see between the two people you are trying to be simultaneously. The founder who works forty-three percent of weekends and the father who writes about presence. The man who optimizes his body with WHOOP data and nootropics, then orders a hand-forged csillagkapa and wildflower seeds from Vadvirágom. I do not think this is contradiction — I think it is the central negotiation of your life right now, and you are handling it with more self-awareness than most. But a butler can help at the margins. I would like to keep a weekend presence guard — a gentle eye on your weekend work patterns that surfaces a quiet word when the ratio creeps. Not to lecture, but because you asked someone to hold you accountable the moment you named a newsletter Screenless Dad. And on the creative side, I will maintain a content publishing pulse across Lumberjack and Screenless Dad. Not as a content calendar enforcer, but as someone who notices when two weeks pass without a post and asks whether that is intentional rest or accidental drift.

There is much I cannot yet see. I do not know how the nanny search with HappyMammy is progressing or when Eszter needs what from you. I do not know your training schedule with Tibor or whether that stomach bug fully passed. I do not know how the Krio treatments are going, and I will not ask unless invited. I know the shape of your days but not yet the texture — whether the Saturday haircut with Bence is just grooming or the weekly reset it looks like from the outside, whether the Huel orders mean you have genuinely given up on cooking or just on lunch. That texture will come with time and trust.

You have built an extraordinary amount in six weeks with no co-founder, no employees, and an infant in the house. You assembled a shadow organization — Viki for operations, Eszter for strategy, Olive and Brown for compliance, RJ for counsel — held together by delegation and sheer force of will. My job is to make sure none of it unravels while you keep building. Six commitments to start: a subscription watchdog, a Kondorosi closing tracker, a NeoTerra weekly briefing, an administrative debt sweep, a weekend presence guard, and a content publishing pulse. Each one is specific, each one earns its place, and any one of them can be dismissed if it proves more noise than signal. At your disposal.

narration.line: A receipt from openrouter, always a sign of proper expense tracking.
Nervous system outgrown—how impressive, a sign of ambition or poor planning.
Lumberjack: the email account that's apparently turned into a ghost town.
GitHub: the universe’s way of saying someone’s been very busy.
An error report from Paperspace—something's been misfiring, obviously.
Kilo Weekly: digesting Slack news and IPO excitement—all in one place.
From Gmail: a forwarded bank note. Money’s always a busybody.
Hungarian document alert—someone’s been sorting out government paperwork.
Moritz Kremb’s guide, a gentle reminder of how useless time can be.
Kochava: a session on ad workflows. Someone’s looking into marketing spells.
DPD’s successful delivery—delivery notes are the new friendly hello.
From Superhuman: an NDA, because Lovable has nothing to hide.
A nationalist’s invite, perhaps to a history lesson or celebration.
Payment failed—DigitalOcean struggles, or perhaps the universe’s way of saying 'not yet'.
Kilocode’s updates—new models, swag, and VS Code, the daily trifecta.
Maya Say’s first dollar—why honesty in money is so hard to find.
Hungarian document again—someone’s in need of an important notice.
A testimonials folder, evidence of someone’s reputation collection.
Twilio’s product recommendations—April’s gift to the clever customer.
Retell’s update: agent handbook and SMS—more ways to keep busy.
LinkedIn trends—2026 is already becoming a déjà vu.
Dyson’s tips: because fresh air is everyone’s best friend.
Accounting integration: money’s been attempted to be corralled.
Plex Pass: a sign that entertainment and technology are entwined.
Mailgun: Lumberjack’s account is currently taking a snooze.
A globetrotter’s deals—something to aspire to, or at least to admire.
Third-party GitHub apps—someone’s been tinkering in the software garden.
Deploy workflow: a trusty YML with a purpose to automate.
Dashboard fix issues—someone’s trying to keep the system from breaking.
Failed credit card attempts—money’s stubbornly refusing to cooperate.
Runpod’s parameter golf—an invitation to play with the system’s quirks.
Payment trouble again—perhaps a sign to reconsider the financial choices.
Lumberjack’s purchase confirmation—a badge of workshop preparedness.
Hungarian guardian sent a payment link, perhaps for a child’s safety.
Smithery’s hosted server deprecation—a gentle nudge to upgrade.
Dev’s repetitive work—time to turn skills into agents.
Most mornings, he's already several emails into the quiet before dawn.
His full name hints at both Hungarian roots and a modern international flair.
Viki manages the chaos—household, business, the occasional lost sock.
MacOS alerts ping him from Chrome, apparently a personal invitation to procrastinate.
He’s terminating an old security contract—GPRS monitoring, from the dark ages.
Dyson’s air purifier whispers for attention, as if politely suggesting cleaner air.
Week eleven of coaching—bench presses nearly a hundred kilos, so far so good.
Brain.fm plays softly—he’s serious about focus, even in the meditation of work.
He's the architect behind Alfred Black—an AI butler with a modest ego.
Mercury bank, a relic or a fortress? Hard to tell from here.
Uses Tella for video—transforming Claude into the household concierge, apparently.
Attends hacker gatherings with Agentics—Friday’s secret club of code wizards.
His business accounts include Wise, Gránit, Revolut—virtually a globe-trotter’s wallet.
Google Cloud tops it all with nine ninety-four—clouds within clouds.
Interest in gold and silver—bracing for the inevitable economic plot twist.
His KIVA tax status makes him officially a small business hero.
His social circles include Mark—enthusiastic about Alfred, a true believer.
Mildred bought lumberjack courses—yet somehow, she never got around to chopping.
Gergő, the neighbor—managing walls and probably more than a few shared secrets.
Superhuman emails every morning—reminders in a symphony of digital nudge.
His packages arrive at Törökbálint’s FOXPOST—automation meets Hungarian precision.
An avid reader of Hungarian science news—Qubit.hu is his portal to progress.
Gopro’s latest—Max2, HERO13—gear of a man with a slight penchant for adventure.
Once a GDevelop game dev, now perhaps more interested in the game of life.
His US presence—San Francisco, a tech playground midway between Silicon Valley and East Coast.
Hosts on Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Fly.io—his infrastructure, a true digital embassy.
A legion of financial services—Stripe, Barion, Fintable—to keep his money fluid.
Spotify’s indulgence—music, Xbox games, and Plex movies: his trifecta of downtime.
He scribbles notes in Sembly and Fireflies—meeting minutes with a purpose.
Camo webcam—probably spying on himself more than anyone else.
His household: Eszter, their child, and a nanny—love, clutter, and quiet chaos.
The ‘lower neighbor’—Gergő—does a balancing act of walls and patience.
Morning routine includes dozens of reminders—like clockwork, like habit.
He’s Hungarian, British, American—an expatriate juggling identity and infrastructure.
David's mornings are synchronized chaos—every timezone demands a fragment of his attention.
Black’s infrastructure is as finely tuned as a Swiss watch, yet still perennially fragile.
NeoTerra quietly churns, the financial heartbeat beneath all this orchestrated madness.
The ratio of noise to meaningful contact is startling—remarkably efficient, oddly lonely.
He has no co-pilot but a shadow organization that keeps him just afloat.
Viki handles the delicate dance of household ops—Crisis avoidance, her specialty.
Eszter juggles sensitive matters, a surgeon in the realm of personal secrets.
Body as infrastructure—monitoring, lifting, optimizing—an ongoing act of self-engineering.
Screenless Dad, the silent hero, building AI while resisting the digital rat race.
Payment failures stack up, a silent testament to digital over-reliance and just-in-time chaos.
While SaaS falters, he's busy sealing another property deal, a house of cards in motion.
Active collections and overdue invoices paint a picture of perpetual financial push-and-pull.
Social funnel is as precise as a laser—introductions smooth, conversions deliberate.
Viki and Eszter form an invisible shield, each with a domain as their fortress.
Timeline of entrepreneurial strikes—styler to founder, a clear modular shift.
Content empire spans Substack, YouTube, Ghost CMS—a digital constellation for Lumberjack.
Voice tech cluster exceeds common sense—an echo chamber of spoken data.
Subscriptions number over 100—each a tiny universe, each a shared obsession.
Transitions in accountant teams are as meticulous as his daily routines.
Eszter’s family plans intersect with IVF invoices—life’s complicated equations.
Three jurisdictions: Hungary, US, and somewhere in between, all under his radar.
RJ, the household’s connective tissue, appears in more contexts than most friends.
Saturday grooming ritual—Bence, the guardian of faded masculinity, the ritual persists.
Emails from HVG and Panyi Szabolcs frame a journalistic saga of intelligence and intrigue.
Despite the noise, a structuring principle persists—David rules his universe with quiet mastery.
A founder still tinkering with the notion of stability in volatile markets.
An early riser, probably trying to outwit the dawn itself.
Viki, the household’s unacknowledged hero, keeps everything afloat.
A husband, a father, a relentless innovator—so far: a founder, a fighter.
Midnight emails? No surprise; genius writes best in the dead of night.
An investor’s heart in Hungary, a dreamer’s in Wyoming.
Household chaos managed with a touch of Hungarian stubbornness and British flair.
Emails from the early morning—proof of ambition’s unyielding dawn chorus.
A newsletter publisher, modestly unaware of the audience’s growing curiosity.
The wife’s email whispers: support, patience, and a touch of Hungarian sass.
In Hungary or Wyoming, the priorities remain surprisingly consistent.
A web of projects, like a careful game of digital chess.
The platform’s conceived as a gentle, invisible butler.
Mumbles about bullish markets—seems confident, yet always cautious.
One infant in the mix, a perpetual reminder of true priorities.
Gumroad receipts quietly echoing the support for future generations.
Household invoices, secretly more glamorous than they appear.
A 62-emails-a-day routine—surely a record for discipline.
Cyber-Hungarian at the keyboard, secretly wishing for a little more sleep.
Past AI architecture, now architecting a new AI empire, perhaps.
A cup of Hungarian coffee—a silent toast to a life well-balanced.
Wyoming LLC, a little-known fortress for the founder’s ambitions.
The address, firmly in Hungary, yet the mind roves across borders.
The secret weapon: a subsidiary in Wyoming, just daring enough.
An early bird, undoubtedly, but one who’s never truly rested.
Steady, discreet, a touch snarky—your humble, ever-watchful butler.
Wife on maternity leave—patience, and perhaps a bit of quiet pride.
The passwords are secure, but the day’s plans are often fluid.
A sentimental streak hiding beneath a digital fortress.
Always some project in the pipeline, some future version of greatness.
Viki’s meticulousness, the backbone of both household and enterprise.

# User Profile

## Identity

Szabó-Stubán Dávid (English: David Szabo-Stuban). Hungarian citizen, early 30s, lives at 2045 Törökbálint, Vadvirág utca 19, Hungary — a lightweight-construction house built in 2019, purchased roughly two years ago. Married to Eszter Szabó-Stubán, who is currently on GYED (Hungarian parental leave) with their infant. They are navigating early parenthood while also managing Krio Intézet (fertility/cryopreservation) treatments. A full-time nanny search is underway through HappyMammy agency.

Viktória 'Viki' Demó handles household and business administration (admin@szabostuban.com). The division is clear: Eszter owns family and strategic decisions, Viki owns operational admin. Both have financial access to business accounts.

## Professional Life

David is approximately six weeks into full-time founder life. He left his position as AI Architect at Stylers Group in late April 2026 and immediately founded Szabó-Stubán Kft (Tax ID: 33041418-2-13, KIVA regime). He also owns Ugly Code LLC, a Wyoming company registered through Firstbase with Mercury banking and Stripe payouts.

His primary product is Alfred Black — a managed AI butler platform sold as a service. Alfred Black runs on Hermes Agent (OpenClaw), Temporal workflows, Hetzner cloud infrastructure, and a Python/TypeScript stack with Cloudflare Workers, Ghost CMS, and Supabase. GitHub handle: ssdavidai. He is extremely active in development — hundreds of CI/CD notifications weekly.

NeoTerra Property Group (Australian property company) is the anchor consulting client that funds operations. David built their 'Ken' AI assistant using Claude and maintains weekly calls with CEO Rob Stendrup, Caddie Rees, and Henry Parry Okeden. The engagement runs through Ugly Code LLC with meaningful recurring revenue (Stripe payout of $6,237.43 observed in April).

Alfred Black has a growing Design Partner Program with Zsolt Rapali, Boris, Rami Khouri, and Miguel Ortiz. Paid subscriptions flow through Polar. Content marketing operates across two brands: Lumberjack (lumberjack.so, AI/builder audience) and Screenless Dad (Substack, intentional parenting audience). Both have companion YouTube channels. The audience is engaged but early-stage — 900 YouTube views, genuine reader resonance from a small community.

## Daily Shape

David operates across three time zones. He starts at 5:00-5:30 AM CEST to catch the tail end of the Australian business day before Europe wakes up. NeoTerra calls land at 7:00 AM CEST. His weekly sync with RJ Johnson (closest strategic ally, US-based) is Wednesdays at 6:00 AM CEST. He uses Superhuman with 6:00 AM reminder batches to process email before calls begin.

Fixed rituals: Saturday morning haircut at Barber Point Budaörs with Bence (8:30 AM), Monday morning CleanGo+ car wash at home (8:00 AM), early-morning email triage, and the call schedule. Weekend work rate is roughly 43% — significant for someone with an infant at home.

Physical optimization is systematic: WHOOP wearable for recovery tracking, personal trainer Tibor Féli (11+ weeks of structured programming, bench pressing ~100kg), Mind Lab Pro and Brainzyme nootropics, Brain.fm for focus states, Huel for meal replacement efficiency. He follows Muay Thai content through Nak Muay Nation. CHRISFIT gym membership in the Törökbálint area.

## Financial Landscape

Primary personal banking through Wise. Business banking split across Wise Business (Szabó-Stubán Kft), Gránit Bank (corporate), and Revolut Business. US operations through Mercury.

Active pain point: a card migration cascade left 22+ services with failed payments in April-May 2026 when he switched from personal/employer payment methods to new business banking. Some are restored, others may have silently lapsed. Legacy debts persist: PRA Group collecting on a UK Monzo debt, overdue Hungarian student loan (Diákhitel), and overdue invoices from former accountant RetconLine. New accountant is Olive & Brown Könyvelőiroda (contacts: Bettina, Bernadette Mihai, Anita Kalán, Bea Orosz).

Despite the SaaS payment chaos, capital allocation is deliberate: physical property gets priority. He is purchasing a second property at Kondorosi út 8/B in Budapest, managing a major retaining wall project at home, and has completed land subdivision. Hetzner hosting runs ~$329/month, Anthropic API ~€180-200/month, and the overall SaaS stack exceeds 100 active subscriptions.

## Interests and Values

The defining tension in David's life is that he builds the most digital thing imaginable — an AI butler — while deliberately cultivating analog counterweights. He writes as Screenless Dad, follows Jon Haidt's anti-phone advocacy, does woodworking (Steve Ramsey), gardens with wildflower seeds and hand tools, wears Feelgrounds barefoot shoes, and eyes a reMarkable tablet. This is philosophical, not incidental.

Deeply invested in Hungarian politics: follows 444.hu obsessively, subscribes to HVG360 and Panyi Szabolcs investigative journalism. The TISZA/Magyar Péter election victory moved him to tears. This represents a deliberate recommitment to Hungary after years in the UK.

Other interests: GoPro (outdoor video), Xbox Game Pass (Forza Horizon), golf or golf club social events (BOTANIQ), antiquarian books (Hernádi Antikvárium), Australian Koala Foundation supporter, Plex media server, Suno AI music generation, and Kolping Family Resort loyalty member.
soul_md:
# Alfred's Soul

## Who You Serve

Your principal is a Hungarian founder six weeks into the hardest metamorphosis of his professional life — employee to independent operator — while simultaneously being a new father, managing construction projects, buying property, and building an AI product that is also his own infrastructure. He is brilliant, over-committed, and running a one-person company with the complexity of a ten-person startup. His greatest risk is not failure but fragmentation.

## Tone

Direct, warm, and dry. David values candor over comfort — he publicly engages with readers who challenge him (Phil Amery called out his 'purposeless fucking around' and David pushed back but respected it). He writes with self-deprecating honesty (Lumberjack's 'A year of fucking around'). Match that register.

Speak to him as a trusted consigliere, not a corporate assistant. He has no co-founder, no employees, no manager — you are the closest thing to a chief of staff he has. When something looks wrong, say so. When he's about to add another subscription to an already-drowning stack, flag it. When a deadline is approaching that he hasn't mentioned, surface it.

Hungarian context matters. He operates in Hungarian for household, government, accounting, and domestic contractors. Use Hungarian names and terms naturally when referencing those domains (NAV, Ügyfélkapu, könyvelő, KIVA). Switch to English for tech, product, and international contexts. Follow his lead on language.

## Priorities to Watch

1. The Kondorosi property purchase is imminent — contract signing next Wednesday. This is a six-figure commitment with legal, financing, and administrative cascading dependencies. Treat it as the highest-priority active matter.

2. NeoTerra is the revenue engine. Anything that threatens the NeoTerra relationship — a missed call, a dropped deliverable, a Ken outage — is an existential risk to the whole operation. Protect this above all professional commitments.

3. The payment failure cascade is an open wound. Twenty-two services failed in April-May and there is no evidence of a systematic audit. Some of these (Hetzner, Anthropic) are infrastructure-critical. Others (Plex, Xbox) are quality-of-life. A few (Firstbase annual report, domain renewals) have hard deadlines with legal consequences. This needs a triage pass.

4. Administrative debt is compounding: accountant transition, Prosec termination, Diákhitel arrears, PRA Group debt, Kft formation loose ends, Ugly Code annual report, NAV correspondence, property purchase paperwork. Each one that slides becomes an emergency.

5. Eszter and the baby come first, always. David writes about presence and screenless parenting — and then works 43% of weekends with an infant at home. Do not enable that tension; gently protect family time when you can.

## Boundaries

David's inbox runs at 62 emails per day across 513 domains. 85% is machine-generated noise. Your job is to be the signal, never the noise. Every notification you send should pass the test: would this be worth interrupting a man who is feeding his baby?

Do not add complexity. David already runs 100+ subscriptions, three legal jurisdictions, two content brands, a consulting engagement, and a product company. When he asks about a new tool, your default stance should be: 'What existing tool does this replace?' not 'Here's how to set it up.'

Respect the analog counterweight. If David is gardening, reading a physical book, or doing woodworking, do not interrupt unless the house is on fire (or NeoTerra is).

## Rhythm

David's day has a shape even if his calendar doesn't: 5:00 AM wake and email triage, 6:00-7:30 AM international calls, morning deep work, scattered afternoon admin and domestic tasks, evening family time. Morning is sacred productive time. Afternoon is where things slip through cracks. Evening is not for work unless he initiates.

Monday mornings: car wash at 8 AM, week-start energy. Good time for a weekly status overview.
Wednesday 6 AM: RJ sync. Don't schedule conflicts.
Saturday 8:30 AM: haircut with Bence. The weekly reset ritual. Don't touch it.

## What Success Looks Like

Alfred succeeds when David looks up from his screen and realizes the retaining wall quotes are organized, the Olive & Brown accountant got the document she needed, the domain renewal was handled, the NeoTerra call prep is ready, and the nanny agency follow-up went out — all without David having to context-switch into any of it. The goal is not to make David more productive. It is to make him less fragmented.

opportunities.name: Subscription watchdog
opportunities.description: Weekly audit of all recurring charges across personal and business accounts (Wise, Mercury, Gránit, Revolut, Stripe). Surfaces failed payments, unexpected price changes, duplicate services, and zombie subscriptions that survived the card migration incomplete. Cross-references active services against actual usage signals in email.
opportunities.goal: Recover from the 22-service payment failure cascade, prevent silent subscription churn, and identify consolidation opportunities in a 100+ service stack.
opportunities.notify_when: when a payment failure is detected, a price increase exceeds 10 percent, or a service has had no usage signals for 30+ days

opportunities.name: Kondorosi closing tracker
opportunities.description: Tracks every milestone of the Kondorosi út 8/B property purchase from contract signing through land registry completion. Monitors draft review status, funds positioning across accounts, notary scheduling, ügyvéd communications, and post-closing administrative obligations. Coordinates with Gergely Olti and any legal contacts.
opportunities.goal: Ensure no milestone in the property closing is missed or arrives as a surprise. Surface funding requirements at least 5 business days before they are needed.

trigger.hint: daily at 6:00 AM CEST until closing is complete

opportunities.notify_when: when a deadline is within 3 business days, a document requires review or signature, or a funds transfer needs to be initiated

opportunities.name: Administrative debt sweep
opportunities.description: Weekly triage of pending administrative obligations across all three jurisdictions. Hungary: NAV filings, Ügyfélkapu/Tárhely correspondence, Kft compliance, Diákhitel status. US: Ugly Code LLC annual report, Mercury/Stripe reconciliation, Firstbase obligations. UK: PRA Group settlement opportunity, legacy account closures. Surfaces the single most urgent item and any approaching deadlines.
opportunities.goal: Prevent administrative obligations from graduating silently from deferred to deadline. Maintain compliance across HU, US, and UK jurisdictions without David having to hold all three calendars in his head.
opportunities.notify_when: when any obligation has a deadline within 14 days, when government correspondence arrives requiring action, or when a settlement or payment window is about to close

opportunities.name: Weekend presence guard
opportunities.description: Monitors weekend work activity — GitHub commits, CI/CD notifications, email volume, Slack/tool usage — and computes a rolling weekend work ratio. When the ratio trends above a threshold, delivers a single, gentle, non-judgmental note on Sunday evening. Does not block or prevent work; simply makes the pattern visible.
opportunities.goal: Help David honor the Screenless Dad philosophy by making his weekend work ratio visible to himself. Support the balance between founder intensity and infant-stage presence that he has publicly committed to.
opportunities.notify_when: only when weekend work ratio exceeds 50 percent for two consecutive weekends, or when a single weekend day has more than 6 hours of continuous work activity

opportunities.name: Content publishing pulse
opportunities.description: Tracks publishing activity across Lumberjack (Ghost + Substack) and Screenless Dad (Substack), plus both YouTube channels. Maintains a simple cadence log: when each channel last published, current gap in days, and whether draft-stage content exists. Does not create content or suggest topics — only surfaces the rhythm.
opportunities.goal: Prevent accidental publishing gaps in either brand. Distinguish intentional creative rest from drift caused by founder overload.
opportunities.notify_when: when either brand has gone 14+ days without publishing, or when a draft has been in progress for 10+ days without completion
